text:
alex: Heads-up — turned on fused RoPE + paged-FlashAttention in the staging pool and saw p95 latency jump ~2x for chat workloads when batch sizes hit ~24. KV cache write stalls in the trace. Anyone seen this combo before? :thinking:

sasha: Can you paste the microbench numbers + config you used?

alex: Quick paste below:
```
model_variant: flash-paged-fused-rope-v2
batching: dynamic
max_batch: 32
kv_cache: paged
rotary_dims: 64
rotary_scale: per-dim
```
bench (single-GPU, seq=1024): p50=11.8ms p95=53.2ms throughput=310tok/s
staging (multi-GPU, burst): p50=14ms p95=110ms throughput=~220tok/s (noticed stutter spikes)

perf-bot: regression-detect: alert for repo/redwood-serving @ 1908000009 commit 4a7c2f6 — latency +45% vs baseline on paged+fused-rope profile. Link: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/1908000009

jamie: Interesting, I ran a microbench with synthetic KV ops and saw write contention when page eviction frequency > 0.6. Flame graph shows long GPU memcpy/host-sync around KV flush.

kevin: My hypothesis: fused RoPE implementation changed memory layout for rotary dims (interleaved vs blocked) and that increases the working set for KV pages during attention recompute. At batch ~24 we cross L2/L3 thresholds causing extra copies.

kevin: simple thought: if rotary_scale is applied per-dim it touches more cache lines. Try rotary_scale: per-head or reduce rotary_dims to 32 to see effect.

alex: Tried rotary_dims=32 on same staging run: p95 down to ~62ms (was 110ms). Throughput up ~15%. Not ideal but confirms sensitivity.

maria: Can you attach the perftrace? Also run `tools/repro/run_paged_kv_probe.sh --seq 1024 --batch 24 --variant flash-paged-fused-rope-v2` and upload `perf.json`. I'll spin a canary with a patched allocator.

alex: Uploaded trace: https://artifacts.redwood/local/1908000011/trace.zip — highlights: repeated KV write stall at attention layer 7, timeline shows host->device sync every ~18ms.

jamie: Patch idea: change batching heuristic to prefer smaller batching window for paged-KV models (max-inflight per-GPU = ceil(GPU_mem / working_set_est)). I ran a simulation and for our profiles it reduces p95 by ~20% at cost of 3% throughput.

kevin: Another angle: alter fused kernel to operate on blocked rotary layout when rotary_dims > 48. That avoids the extra stride and reduces cache line churn. Might be nontrivial but predictable.

maria: Ops ask: if we change batching heuristic we avoid kernel changes and get fast rollback. Could be ops-config toggle. But we need unit tests to catch perf regressions.

alex: Agreed. For immediate mitigation I'll flip `batching.window_ms=8` for paged-KV fleets and schedule kernel fix work.

perf-bot: canary-deploy started for fleet "staging-paged-kv" at 1908000035. Will watch p95 for 30m.

jamie: I'll open a PR with the heuristic and a microbench harness that runs the reproduce script in CI (non-blocking). Link when ready.

kevin: I'll prototype blocked-rotary kernel in a branch, compare memory ops with nvprof. If that looks good we can upstream.

maria: Good plan. Action items: jamie heuristic PR, kevin kernel prototype, alex monitor canary + attach perf logs. Ping me if canary p95 stays > 1.5x baseline after 30m.

alex: Thanks — will update thread with canary summary at 1908000065. :thumbsup:
